item.title: Student Recital - Andrew Milburn — Nov 14, 2026
item.description:
Strauss Performing Arts Center Saturday, November 14, 2026 · 6:30 PM On Saturday, November 14, at 6:30 Andrew Milburn will perform a senior voice recital at the Strauss Performing Arts Center’s Recital Hall on the University of Nebraska at Omaha’s campus. Andrew will perform a variety of classical works. Marissa Mathia will appear as collaborative pianist.
Andrew Milburn (voice) is a student of Dr. Jennifer Townsley. Andrew’s previous collegiate instructors included Alisa Belflower, Dalan Guthrie, and Alexandria Plumb. In his junior year, Andrew was awarded the Ruetz Scholarship for voice at the UNO School of Music. During his time in Omaha, he has performed throughout the greater Omaha area as part of the Opera Omaha chorus, an Alumni performer for Omaha Performing Arts, and leading roles in the UNO Opera such as The Miller and Don Alfonso. Andrew most recently appeared with the UNO Concert Choir as a member and section leader in their Fall concert. Looking forward, Andrew hopes to pursue a Master’s degree. Source: UNO School of Music

item.title: Scary Stories — Oct 30, 2026
item.description:
Simon Concert Hall at the Omaha Conservatory of Music Friday, October 30, 2026 · 7:00 PM @
Friday, October 30, 2026, 7:00 PMSimon Concert Hall, Omaha Conservatory of MusicDoors open at 6:30 PM. Free and open to the public.
Spend the night before Halloween with us. Scary Stories gathers the music that has been giving audiences goosebumps for two hundred years, from a desperate midnight ride through the forest to a witches’ gathering on a bare mountaintop.Pianist Tammy Miller-Ladd joins us for Liszt’s Totentanz, a ferocious set of variations on the medieval “Day of Wrath” chant and one of the great showpieces for piano and orchestra.
Costumes are welcome, for kids and adults alike! The orchestra will be dressed up in their halloween best too.
Like every Orchestra Omaha concert, this one is free!
Program
Schubert: Erlkonig
Mussorgsky: Night on Bald Mountain
Liszt: Totentanz, featuring Tammy Miller-Ladd, piano
Lloyd Webber: Selections from The Phantom of the Opera
Grieg: In the Hall of the Mountain King
“Remember Me,” from Coco
Also featuring our Art of Music program
Soloist
Tammy Miller-Ladd, piano
2024 National Finalist, The American PrizeErnst Bacon Memorial Award for the Performance of American Music
Pianist Tammy Miller-Ladd enjoys a multi-faceted career as a soloist, collaborative artist, composer, and educator. She has given presentations, recitals, and masterclasses at colleges, universities, and prestigious concert venuesthroughout the U.S. and abroad. In 2024, Tammy was selected as a National Finalist for the American Prize: Ernst Bacon Memorial Award for the Performance of American Music in the Professional Soloists and Composers Division. In June2018, she made her Kennedy Center debut (D.C.) in a duo recital with famed contraforte soloist, Lewis Lipnick and in 2022, she was invited to be the first ever guest artist for the “En Vivo” Concert Series at the University of Texasat San Antonio.
As a concerto soloist, Tammy has appeared alongside the Bemidji Symphony Orchestra (MN), Springfield Symphony Orchestra (OH), Symphony of the Vines (CA), Westminster College Symphony (PA), Orchestra Omaha (NE), Oklahoma ComposersOrchestra (OK), Dordt University Symphonic Band (IA), and the Lakeland Civic Orchestra (OH). In 2024, she was the soloist for the 100-year anniversary performance of Gershwin’s iconic “Rhapsody in Blue” with the Nebraska Wind Symphonyto great acclaim by concert reviewers: “I was hypnotized by Tammy’s incredible skill and dexterity on this challenging work! She dazzled the audience with her amazing execution of virtually every technique required of the virtuosopianist… lightning speed octaves and repeated notes, interlocking hand passages, and arpeggiated figures…”. – Mark Dickmeyer, OTMA President. She has commissioned and given the world premiere of piano concertos by Daniel Perttu(2019 & 2023), Eric Ewazen (2023), and Stephanie Ann Boyd is writing her Conservation Concerto, “Orchidelirium” for Tammy to premiere in 2026.
As a composer, Tammy’s largest work to date is her cycle, “Learning to…” written for soprano and piano. The collection was the subject of a 166-page dissertation “A Performance Guide to Tammy Miller’s Learning To… A Song Cycle onthe Experience of Grief in Five Poems by Mary Oliver” (2021). Selections from her “Sea Songs” for mezzo-soprano and piano, based on the poetry of American Lyric poet, Sara Teasdale, were premiered in 2023 at the Mostly Modern Festivalin Saratoga Springs, New York. She has also completed a collection of works for intermediate pianists titled “Bedtime Stories: An Album for the Young” which was commissioned by Dr. Ivan Hurd with funds provided by the University ofTexas – San Antonio.
This December, she will travel to Prague, Czech Republic as the featured soloist for the world premiere recording of her “War Songs: There Will Come Soft Rains” under the baton of British conductor Mikel Toms, in collaboration withthe Czech Studio Orchestra.
As a passionate educator, Tammy has taught students in individual and group piano lessons at the collegiate and pre-collegiate levels. Her students have won numerous prizes at local and state competitions and several student have beenaccepted to music programs with generous scholarship offers at prestigious colleges and universities across the midwest. In 2022, Tammy was a recognized as a “Yamaha 40 under 40” music educator, one of four piano teachers across thenation that hold this distinction.
Tammy earned a performance degree with concentrations in piano and voice from Idaho State University (B.M.) and a piano performance and pedagogy degree from the University of Oklahoma (M.M.). Her primary teachers included Dr. KoriBond, Virginia Willard, Bev Beck, Dr. Jeongwon Ham, and pedagogy studies with famed pedagogue Dr. Jane Magrath. She currently serves as piano artist-faculty at the InterHarmony International Music Festival in Acqui Terme, Italy.
